key_insight: QD-PINN uses physics-informed neural networks to estimate optimal stopping boundaries for Bayesian quickest detection in high-dimensional, spatially dependent diffusion processes.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a potential route to computationally tractable change-detection policies when conventional variational-inequality solvers struggle in high dimensions.
method: Learn stopping boundaries through a physics-informed neural network framework.
Establish an equivalence between the free-boundary PDE and infinite-dimensional stochastic optimization.
Assess boundary uncertainty using deep ensembles and Monte Carlo dropout.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with available reference numerical solutions and low boundary variability across independent training runs and stochastic forward passes.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative accuracy, runtime, or dimensional-scaling results, so practical scalability remains difficult to assess.
paper_title: QD-PINN:A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Bayesian Quickest Detection in High-Dimensional Diffusions
